acceptance.claim: On the Owner, Hirer and Driver forms a 'Redirect' button is shown from the loaded record (the particulars exist and that person is not the current offender); it does not depend on an ID typed by the officer. The flow has two confirmations: a first modal, then the form unlocks in REDIRECT mode (name, ID type, e-mail, phone and address can be edited and form validation is skipped), then a second modal 'Do you wish to proceed to Redirect the Notice?'.
acceptance.missing: Button condition, two modals, skipped validation are proved. NOT proved: 'ID type ... can be edited'. On the Owner and Driver forms the ID type dropdown and the ID number input are locked unless mode is CREATE (OwnerForm.tsx:290,301; DriverForm.tsx:299,310), so in REDIRECT mode ID type and ID number cannot be changed there; the Hirer form was not confirmed. Roles that can open the Notice form: cannot verify from repo (server side only maps the two endpoints to OCMS_OIC_FURNISH).
acceptance.fix_en: On the Owner, Hirer and Driver forms a 'Redirect' button is shown when the loaded record exists and that person is not the current offender (hasParticulars && !isOffender); it does not depend on an ID typed by the officer. Two confirmations apply: a first modal, then the form unlocks in REDIRECT mode (name, e-mail, phone and address can be edited; on the Owner and Driver forms the ID type and ID number stay locked; form validation is skipped), then a second modal 'Do you wish to proceed to Redirect the Notice?'.

acceptance.claim: On confirm the system finds the target record by notice number and owner/driver indicator, checks that the ID number matches the stored one (otherwise 'ID number does not match'), sets every row with offender_indicator 'Y' to 'N' and the target to 'Y'; the particulars submitted on the form (name, ID type, e-mail, phone, address) are written onto the target record in the same call; name and ID type are mandatory.
acceptance.missing: Core swap (find target, ID match, all Y -> N, target Y) is proved. The particulars are written conditionally: name/ID type only if non-blank, e-mail and phone only if not null, and the address is written to the furnished_mail address row (createOrUpdateFurnishedMailAddress) only when address fields are supplied, not onto the offender row. The error text in the code is 'ID number does not match the target offender record'. From the staff UI the ID type and ID number are locked (OwnerForm.tsx:290,301), so the UI resubmits the stored ID type.
acceptance.fix_en: On confirm the system finds the target record by notice number and owner/driver indicator, checks that the submitted ID number equals the stored one (otherwise 'ID number does not match the target offender record'), sets every row with offender_indicator 'Y' to 'N' and the target to 'Y'. In the same call the submitted name and ID type (both mandatory) are written to the target record, e-mail and phone are written when supplied, and the address is written to the furnished_mail address record when address fields are supplied.

acceptance.claim: The redirect is refused when the notice is not furnishable (checkFurnishable, for example a PS/LPS suspension blocks it) and when the submitted ID type is a UEN (B or U) for a Driver; the UEN check reads the ID type of the request, not the stored record.
acceptance.missing: UEN-for-Driver block is proved and reads request.getIdType(). The furnishable check is proved, but 'PS/LPS suspension' is wrong wording: the check blocks only an ACTIVE PERMANENT suspension (PS, date_of_revival null), the Advisory Notice flag, and a last processing stage outside FURNISHABLE_STAGES (NPA, ROV, ENA, RD1, RD2, RR3, DN1, DN2, DR3, CFC, CPC). A temporary suspension (TS) does not block. 'LPS' in the code comments means Last Processing Stage, not a suspension.
acceptance.fix_en: The redirect is refused when the notice is not furnishable (checkFurnishable: an active Permanent Suspension (PS), the Advisory Notice flag, or a last processing stage outside the furnishable list), and when the submitted ID type is a UEN (B or U) for a Driver; the UEN check reads the ID type of the request, not the stored record.

acceptance.missing: Fee reset is tied to OCMS-DF-2026-170 only by a code comment (SV line 412). Amount: no rule in applyCalculationRules gives a fee for target RD1/DN1 (all matching rules return formatAmount(compositionAmount); default is also composition) - read in full, not a single line.

overlap.reason: 41.46 is record/update particulars. The redirect call (staffRedirect) rewrites name, ID type, e-mail, phone and address of the target in the same call, the UI reuses the same forms and the same ODH update mapping (MapPostOffenceNoticeODH mode UPDATE). Same points (3). URA can read 52.6 as a second claim of 41.46 unless the claim is limited to the switch of the current offender plus stage reset.

41.47 is the confirm/overwrite prompt. 52.6 has its own two modals (redirect confirm and proceed), which look similar to an overwrite confirmation; the redirect confirm is a separate modal (showRedirectConfirm) but the intent (confirm before changing a record) overlaps.

41.44 is checking furnishable stage and prompting existing particulars. 52.6 reuses staff-furnish/furnish-redirect-check and the hasParticulars display; only the switch of the current offender is new.
